name: Indian independence movement
title: The story of the Indian independence movement

text: About 140 years ago, while Britain ruled India, educated Indians formed the Indian National Congress to ask for reforms.
One of them, Dadabhai Naoroji, argued that British rule was draining away India’s wealth.
src: By the 1880s Britain ruled India through the British Raj / 1885: The Indian National Congress holds its first session in Bombay / Begun by educated Indians seeking reform
Dadabhai Naoroji, a Parsi from Bombay, argued that British rule drained India’s wealth

text: Mahatma Gandhi led huge non-violent campaigns, protests without fighting, that drew in millions of people.
On the Salt March, he walked with 78 followers to Dandi, where he made salt to defy a British tax.
src: the Indian National Congress grew under Mahatma Gandhi into a mass movement whose non-violent campaigns drew millions into the struggle against British rule
Gandhi began the Salt March, walking with 78 followers some 385 kilometres from his ashram at Sabarmati to Dandi, where on 6 April he made salt in defiance of the salt tax

text: British troops sometimes fired on unarmed crowds, and many leaders, among them Jawaharlal Nehru, were put in prison.
Women joined in great numbers, making salt and standing outside shops in protest.
src: Troops fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds / The Congress launches the Quit India Movement, and its leaders are imprisoned / Jawaharlal Nehru
Women came forward in great numbers from 1930, making salt, picketing shops and courting arrest

text: Indians did not all agree on what freedom should look like.
The Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, asked for separate states where most people were Muslims.
src: It was never one body: moderates, radicals, revolutionaries, the Muslim League, peasants, workers, opponents of caste and the people of the princely states pursued different, often conflicting aims
in the Lahore Resolution of March 1940 the League under Muhammad Ali Jinnah demanded “independent states” for the Muslim-majority areas

text: More than 75 years ago British rule ended, and British India was split into two countries, India and Pakistan.
About fifteen million people had to leave their homes, and very many were killed in the fighting that followed.
src: 1947: British rule ends, and British India is partitioned into India and Pakistan
which uprooted some fifteen million people and was accompanied by killings on a vast scale

text: Gandhi’s way of peaceful protest was later studied by Martin Luther King Jr. in the United States.
Today India and Pakistan each celebrate their independence day in August.
src: Gandhi’s methods of non-violent resistance were studied by the leaders of the civil rights movement in the United States, among them Martin Luther King Jr.
India celebrates its independence on 15 August and honours Gandhi as the Father of the Nation, while Pakistan celebrates 14 August
